function: no_learning, pp. 1, 9-10: variational-inference message passing (GAMP detection, mean-field gain estimation, EM gradient-descent sensing); 'federated learning' is distributed per-frame estimation of UE position/velocity, no trained model.
notes: The PDF matches the DOI: p. 1 gives the title 'Integrated Sensing and Communication Receiver Design for OTFS-Based MIMO System: A Unified Variational Inference Framework' and 'Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/JSAC.2025.3531574'. Step 1: it is a research article that proposes and evaluates a method, so neither source_type nor survey applies, but it fails no_learning. The receiver is variational-inference message passing, p. 1: 'belief propagation, mean field, and expectation maximization algorithms for data detection, channel coefficient estimation, and kinematic parameter sensing are derived'. Sensing is gradient descent on a likelihood objective, p. 9: 'we can learn parameters p by exploiting gradient descent algorithms for problem (74)'. The 'federated learning' scheme only splits that estimation across base stations, p. 10: '(74) is optimized in a distributed manner with the kinematic parameter p representing a global model learned from aggregated local parameters'. Here the 'model' is the UE position and velocity of the current frame, initialized 'with coarse on-grid search' (p. 10, Algorithm 2). No neural network, training set, or trained parameter appears anywhere in the paper. Aggregation is digital over backhaul links, not over the air (p. 3: 'connected to the processing unit (i.e., CPU or DPU) via backhaul links'; p. 10: 'the local gradients are transmitted to the CPU'), so the exception for federated learning over the air does not apply. Even if the federated scheme were counted as learning, it performs localization with digital aggregation, which would be excluded under function. The baselines are JCEDD-NLS and the perfect-communication and perfect-sensing bounds (p. 11), and none of them is learned.
